compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`infra/scripts/observability.sh` counts journal/log markers CUMULATIVELY — grep the whole
journal for a token, publish `total - prev`, where `prev` is a persisted offset file. Six
counters share the shape, and every one guards the negative case identically:

    new=$((total - prev))
    [ "$new" -lt 0 ] && new=$total

Verified present at §3 replication_errors, §4 voter_errors, §4c
review_bot_merge_change_errors, §4d deploy_errors, §4e (the shared
`publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` helper, covering deploy_deferrals AND review_interrupts),
and §4b g2p_dispatch_errors.

A negative delta happens only when the journal LOSES history it previously had — journald
vacuuming by `SystemMaxUse`/`MaxRetentionSec`, a `journalctl --vacuum-*`, or the persistent
journal being cleared. In exactly that case the guard republishes the ENTIRE remaining count
as "new this interval", re-counting markers already counted and already alarmed on.

## Why it matters most for `review_interrupts`

`rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts` (monitoring_autodeploy.tf) is `period=900,
evaluation_periods=1, datapoints_to_alarm=1, threshold>0` — deliberately a single datapoint so
the `signal-unavailable` case surfaces fast. One spurious republish therefore pages, and it
pages pointing an investigator at journal history that was just deleted.

## NOT currently firing — latent, not the cause of anything observed

Measured on i-00880b2c7f13527c5 on 2026-08-12 while diagnosing [rebar:7b4a-0f39-1a45-4ce9]:
journal total = 7, offset file = 7, journal reaches back to 2026-07-03. No rotation has
occurred on this box yet. Filed because the hazard was ruled OUT by measurement, not design.

## Plan

Minimal, bash-delta-negative-to-flat. Do NOT add a boot-id/cursor state machine: that is real
logic, and this repo prefers deleting bash over growing it (AGENTS.md strangler-fig). The
correct fix is one token per site.

1. Replace the clamp at all six sites with `new=0`, i.e. treat lost history as
   already-counted. Rationale: the offset is monotonic evidence that those markers were
   already published. If the journal shrank, every surviving marker is at-or-older-than the
   ones we already counted, so republishing them is guaranteed double-counting; suppressing
   them under-counts at most the markers emitted inside the single rotating interval. For a
   1-datapoint pager, a missed count that the NEXT interval catches (the offset resets to the
   new smaller total, so genuinely-new markers after rotation still publish) is strictly
   better than a false page. The offset write is unchanged: `echo "$total" > offset` still
   runs on successful publish, so the counter re-bases to the shrunken journal in one interval.
2. State that rationale in the script as a single shared comment at §3 (the first site) and
   a one-line back-reference at the other sites — no duplicated prose.
3. Extend the existing bash-driven pytest harness
   `tests/scripts/test_observability_offsets_6a65.py`'s pattern with a new test module that
   drives the real script with a stubbed `journalctl`/`aws` and a PRE-SEEDED offset file
   LARGER than the stub's marker count (the shrinking-journal simulation), asserting the
   published value is 0 — not the total — for `review_interrupts` and every other counter.

No Python migration is warranted: after this change the counters are a subtraction and a
clamp, not logic worth porting. A future time-windowed (`journalctl --since`) rewrite would
delete the offset files entirely and IS the right shape, but it changes the metric's
semantics under clock skew and is out of scope for a latent-hazard bugfix.

## Deployment

No manual box action. `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` watches `OBS_PATHS`
(`infra/scripts/observability.sh infra/scripts/install-observability.sh`) and re-runs the
idempotent `install-observability.sh` on the box when either changes, re-materializing
`/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh`. Landing on `main` ships it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: No `new=$total` (or per-site equivalent `*new=$*total`) clamp remains in
      `infra/scripts/observability.sh`; all six negative-delta guards assign 0. Verify:
      `grep -nE '(-lt 0 \])? *&& *[a-z]*new=\$[a-z]*total' infra/scripts/observability.sh`
      returns no matches.
- [ ] AC2: A test drives the real script with an offset file seeded ABOVE the journal marker
      count and asserts the published `review_interrupts` value is `0`, covering every one of
      the six counters. Verify: the new test module passes and FAILS against the pre-fix
      script (checked by reverting the clamp locally once).
- [ ] AC3: The chosen behaviour on lost history — suppress rather than republish — is stated
      with its rationale in a comment in `infra/scripts/observability.sh`.
- [ ] AC4: Existing `tests/scripts/test_observability_offsets_6a65.py` and
      `tests/scripts/test_observability_exit.py` still pass (no regression to the
      publish-then-persist-offset contract).

file_impact.reason: Replace the negative-delta clamp new=$total with new=0 at all six cumulative marker counters, plus the rationale comment.
New test: shrinking-journal simulation asserts each counter publishes 0, not the total.
